The first real provision run created three of four resources and reported
success. Two things were wrong with that.

The R2 listing failed with "A request to the Cloudflare API (/accounts/…/
r2/buckets) failed." and nothing else — wrangler puts the code that separates
a missing token scope from a product never enabled on the account on the line
under the marked one, and only the marked one was being read. The reason now
carries its continuation.

And the run went green while production was not ready: the provisioner exits
clean when it declines, which is right, but the preflight after it ran under
`|| true`. The preflight is the honest answer to "did it work"; it now decides
the run.

A concurrency group also queues a second press behind the first, so two runs
cannot both try to create the same resource.

Answers the C-SPAN licensing open question carried by both the market and
competitor wikis, and corrects the claim it supersedes.

C-SPAN's terms forbid any bot, spider or automatic device copying its content
without written permission, and it refuses unlicensed commercial use of its
programming even where the underlying federal event is public domain. The
chamber proceedings are public domain; C-SPAN's archive of them is not an
available source. The government publishes the same material itself —
HouseLive, Congress.gov video, and GPO's govinfo CREC bulk XML and API, whose
data Congress.gov states is public domain.

That backbone carries its own trap: the Congressional Record is not a
transcript. Members may correct their own remarks before publication and may
print material they never spoke on the floor, so a contradiction found between
two Record entries may be a contradiction between two edits.

Also records the substitute academics adopted after the Twitter API shutdown:
the Internet Archive TV News Archive plus GDELT, which splits the data vacuum —
broadcast speech is well-corpused and free, text and social speech are not.

Phase 6 of #34. Pure functions over a series — no store, no model — so a case
can plant a step change or an outlier and assert exactly what comes back.

An anomaly is one utterance out of step, carrying where it was said and to whom.
A trend change reports the interval the step falls in, never a date; without
both ends dated there is no interval and nothing is recorded.

Two things the cases found. The leave-one-out baseline alone reported every point
of a bimodal series as an anomaly — and a bimodal series is what a trend change
looks like — so an anomaly now also has to be alone. And withUtterance collapsed
an explicit null date into its default, which is the failure 1.3 and 1.9 exist to
prevent, sitting in the fixtures.

The third leaf is the silence: a flat series, one too short to have a shape, and
one that drifts without stepping must all come back empty.

Answers the C-SPAN licensing open question carried by both the market and
competitor wikis, and corrects the claim it supersedes.

C-SPAN's terms forbid any bot, spider or automatic device copying its content
without written permission, and it refuses unlicensed commercial use of its
programming even where the underlying federal event is public domain. The
chamber proceedings are public domain; C-SPAN's archive of them is not an
available source. The government publishes the same material itself —
HouseLive, Congress.gov video, and GPO's govinfo CREC bulk XML and API, whose
data Congress.gov states is public domain.

That backbone carries its own trap: the Congressional Record is not a
transcript. Members may correct their own remarks before publication and may
print material they never spoke on the floor, so a contradiction found between
two Record entries may be a contradiction between two edits.

Also records the substitute academics adopted after the Twitter API shutdown:
the Internet Archive TV News Archive plus GDELT, which splits the data vacuum —
broadcast speech is well-corpused and free, text and social speech are not.

Phase 6 of #34. Pure functions over a series — no store, no model — so a case
can plant a step change or an outlier and assert exactly what comes back.

An anomaly is one utterance out of step, carrying where it was said and to whom.
A trend change reports the interval the step falls in, never a date; without
both ends dated there is no interval and nothing is recorded.

Two things the cases found. The leave-one-out baseline alone reported every point
of a bimodal series as an anomaly — and a bimodal series is what a trend change
looks like — so an anomaly now also has to be alone. And withUtterance collapsed
an explicit null date into its default, which is the failure 1.3 and 1.9 exist to
prevent, sitting in the fixtures.

The third leaf is the silence: a flat series, one too short to have a shape, and
one that drifts without stepping must all come back empty.

{"id":32640257251,"name":"product","display_title":"Say why a Cloudflare question could not be asked, and fail the run wh…","workflow_id":339572729,"run_number":53,"run_attempt":1,"event":"push","status":"in_progress","head_branch":"main","head_sha":"5aea4d28b211bd51425c40b13ba2dfb2978676c0","head_commit":{"message":"Say why a Cloudflare question could not be asked, and fail the run when it wasn't (#82)

The first real provision run created three of four resources and reported
success. Two things were wrong with that.

The R2 listing failed with "A request to the Cloudflare API (/accounts/…/
r2/buckets) failed." and nothing else — wrangler puts the code that separates
a missing token scope from a product never enabled on the account on the line
under the marked one, and only the marked one was being read. The reason now
carries its continuation.

And the run went green while production was not ready: the provisioner exits
clean when it declines, which is right, but the preflight after it ran under
`|| true`. The preflight is the honest answer to "did it work"; it now decides
the run.

A concurrency group also queues a second press behind the first, so two runs
cannot both try to create the same resource.

input.title: Ask the account where a Worker would even be published
input.body:
The first deploy ([32640257251](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/actions/runs/32640257251)) got further than any before it — preflight green, migrations `0001`–`0008` applied to the real D1 — and then stopped:

```
? Would you like to register a workers.dev subdomain now?
🤖 Using fallback value in non-interactive context: no
✘ [ERROR] You can either deploy your worker to one or more routes … or register
  a workers.dev subdomain here:
  https://dash.cloudflare.com/<account>/workers/onboarding
```

The account has never registered a workers.dev subdomain, so the Worker had nowhere to be published to. That is a dashboard step, and it is the third of its kind after R2's onboarding — the category I claimed an hour ago probably didn't exist.

### The preflight said production was ready, and it wasn't

That's the defect worth fixing. Every check ran through `wrangler`, and **wrangler has no command for this** — no `wrangler subdomain`, nothing under `triggers`. So the one fact that decided whether a deploy could succeed was the one fact the preflight structurally could not see, and the deploy discovered it *after* moving the schema.

The preflight now reads the account directly for it: `GET /accounts/{id}/workers/subdomain`. That is the only non-wrangler call in the tooling and it is a GET — which is exactly why the wrangler runner stays closed to everything but lists, creates and deploys. It reports the subdomain when there is one, `MISS` with the onboarding link when there isn't, and `??` when the question couldn't be asked, same as everything else.

### The reason arrived with its actionable half cut off

`#82` taught `firstUsefulLine` to take the lines under wrangler's error headline, stopping at the first blank. Wrangler puts the URL it is sending you to *after* a blank line, so the fix landed one line short of the thing you actually need. It now crosses a single blank and stops at two — capped at a few lines, so a whole log can never become the reason.

### Verified

97 tests, typecheck clean. Both new cases were watched failing first — the blank-line case red when the continuation stopped at the first blank, which is what `main` does today. The subdomain read itself needs an account: what it does with a live answer is unproven here, and the next deploy is its proof.

`dev/tools` — `accountRead` (the one GET), `firstUsefulLine` crossing a single blank line, `dashboardUrl` shared rather than spelled twice; the preflight gains the subdomain check and its checks now run async.

Refs #27

Claudinite loaded, 14 packs, 46 checks, 17,500 rule tokens, 25 available skills, 530 personal preference tokens.

## What I need from you: one click. No value comes back to me.

**The short version:** register a workers.dev subdomain on the account. I don't need to know what you pick — the deploy reads the resulting origin back out of `wrangler deploy`'s own output, and [#89](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/pull/89) teaches the preflight to read it from the account API. Nothing gets pasted into the repo or into Actions afterwards.

### What it is

A Cloudflare account has one account-wide label that all its Workers are published under. Deployed Workers are reachable at:

```
<worker name>.<your subdomain>.workers.dev
```

Our Worker is named `hitbut-api` (in [`wrangler.toml`](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/blob/main/wrangler.toml)), so if you register `missingbulb`, the API's public origin becomes `https://hitbut-api.missingbulb.workers.dev`. **That string is the public host of the API** — the site fetches from it, so it's a naming decision with a visible consequence, not a formality.

Your account has never registered one. `wrangler deploy` therefore has nowhere to publish to; it asks interactively, and on a runner "interactive" means the fallback answer `no`, then an error.

### Where to do it

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

Answers the C-SPAN licensing open question carried by both the market and
competitor wikis, and corrects the claim it supersedes.

C-SPAN's terms forbid any bot, spider or automatic device copying its content
without written permission, and it refuses unlicensed commercial use of its
programming even where the underlying federal event is public domain. The
chamber proceedings are public domain; C-SPAN's archive of them is not an
available source. The government publishes the same material itself —
HouseLive, Congress.gov video, and GPO's govinfo CREC bulk XML and API, whose
data Congress.gov states is public domain.

That backbone carries its own trap: the Congressional Record is not a
transcript. Members may correct their own remarks before publication and may
print material they never spoke on the floor, so a contradiction found between
two Record entries may be a contradiction between two edits.

Also records the substitute academics adopted after the Twitter API shutdown:
the Internet Archive TV News Archive plus GDELT, which splits the data vacuum —
broadcast speech is well-corpused and free, text and social speech are not.

Answers the C-SPAN licensing open question carried by both the market and
competitor wikis, and corrects the claim it supersedes.

C-SPAN's terms forbid any bot, spider or automatic device copying its content
without written permission, and it refuses unlicensed commercial use of its
programming even where the underlying federal event is public domain. The
chamber proceedings are public domain; C-SPAN's archive of them is not an
available source. The government publishes the same material itself —
HouseLive, Congress.gov video, and GPO's govinfo CREC bulk XML and API, whose
data Congress.gov states is public domain.

That backbone carries its own trap: the Congressional Record is not a
transcript. Members may correct their own remarks before publication and may
print material they never spoke on the floor, so a contradiction found between
two Record entries may be a contradiction between two edits.

Also records the substitute academics adopted after the Twitter API shutdown:
the Internet Archive TV News Archive plus GDELT, which splits the data vacuum —
broadcast speech is well-corpused and free, text and social speech are not.

Phase 6 of #34. Pure functions over a series — no store, no model — so a case
can plant a step change or an outlier and assert exactly what comes back.

An anomaly is one utterance out of step, carrying where it was said and to whom.
A trend change reports the interval the step falls in, never a date; without
both ends dated there is no interval and nothing is recorded.

Two things the cases found. The leave-one-out baseline alone reported every point
of a bimodal series as an anomaly — and a bimodal series is what a trend change
looks like — so an anomaly now also has to be alone. And withUtterance collapsed
an explicit null date into its default, which is the failure 1.3 and 1.9 exist to
prevent, sitting in the fixtures.

**Nothing. You already did it.** That page is showing you the finished state, not a to-do.

`hitbut-api.**arielra**.workers.dev` — `arielra` *is* the workers.dev subdomain. Registering it is what the onboarding URL existed to do, which is why that URL is now a 404: it's a first-run-only page and there's nothing left to onboard. The two rows on that screen are exactly the two things the deploy ships, both live.

And the pipeline has been running end to end since. The last `product` run on `main` — [32651585842](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/actions/runs/32651585842/job/97224060412), yesterday 16:26 — is **green through every step**:

| step | |
|---|---|
| Does production exist? | ✅ |
| Bring the corpus schema up to date | ✅ |
| Deploy the Worker | ✅ |
| Build the site against the deployed API | ✅ |
| Deploy the site | ✅ |
| **Does what shipped answer?** (smoke) | ✅ |

That last one is the whole point: it fetched both origins after the deploy and asserted they really answer. Two consecutive green `ship main` runs, both since the subdomain existed.

So requirement `7.1` — *"a merge to `main` reaches the deployed site with no human build step"* — is now **observed**, not just claimed. That's [#30](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/30)'s pass condition and [#27](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/27)'s closing condition, both satisfied.

Your production, as of now:

- **API** — `https://hitbut-api.arielra.workers.dev` (12 requests, 9.3 ms)
- **Site** — `https://hitbut.pages.dev`

I can't fetch either from this sandbox to confirm by sight — outbound is restricted here — so I'm reading the smoke test's verdict rather than the pages themselves. The smoke test does exactly the check I'd do: `/api/v1/figures` returns a JSON `items` array, `/api/v1/nope` returns our own 404 envelope (proving it's our Worker and not a placeholder), and the site returns HTML containing `התבטאויות`.

There's also a fair amount I wasn't part of — [#89](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/pull/89) appears to have landed along with #90, #97, #99, #102, #105, #106. I haven't read those.

Want me to close out the paperwork — verify #30's condition properly and close it, and close #27 — and catch up on what landed while I was away?

> ⚠️ Still open: (1) nothing on your side for the subdomain — it's done, and the deploy has been green end to end twice since; (2) [#27](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/27) and [#30](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/30) both look satisfied but neither is closed — say the word and I'll verify and close them; (3) Vectorize, Workers AI and Workflows still outstanding behind [#34](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/34), each likely needing its own account-level enable; (4) two comments on #27 still render as open tasks — I can't edit comments from this session.

```
? Would you like to register a workers.dev subdomain now?
🤖 Using fallback value in non-interactive context: no
✘ [ERROR] You can either deploy your worker to one or more routes … or register
  a workers.dev subdomain here:
  https://dash.cloudflare.com//workers/onboarding
```

The account has never registered a workers.dev subdomain, so the Worker had nowhere to be published to. That is a dashboard step, and it is the third of its kind after R2's onboarding — the category I claimed an hour ago probably didn't exist.

### The preflight said production was ready, and it wasn't

That's the defect worth fixing. Every check ran through `wrangler`, and **wrangler has no command for this** — no `wrangler subdomain`, nothing under `triggers`. So the one fact that decided whether a deploy could succeed was the one fact the preflight structurally could not see, and the deploy discovered it *after* moving the schema.

The preflight now reads the account directly for it: `GET /accounts/{id}/workers/subdomain`. That is the only non-wrangler call in the tooling and it is a GET — which is exactly why the wrangler runner stays closed to everything but lists, creates and deploys. It reports the subdomain when there is one, `MISS` with the onboarding link when there isn't, and `??` when the question couldn't be asked, same as everything else.

### The reason arrived with its actionable half cut off

`#82` taught `firstUsefulLine` to take the lines under wrangler's error headline, stopping at the first blank. Wrangler puts the URL it is sending you to *after* a blank line, so the fix landed one line short of the thing you actually need. It now crosses a single blank and stops at two — capped at a few lines, so a whole log can never become the reason.

### Verified

97 tests, typecheck clean. Both new cases were watched failing first — the blank-line case red when the continuation stopped at the first blank, which is what `main` does today. The subdomain read itself needs an account: what it does with a live answer is unproven here, and the next deploy is its proof.

`dev/tools` — `accountRead` (the one GET), `firstUsefulLine` crossing a single blank line, `dashboardUrl` shared rather than spelled twice; the preflight gains the subdomain check and its checks now run async.

Refs #27

## 1. Convert the deploy workflows to Claudinite tasks

The repo hand-authors three workflows that Claudinite's vendored plumbing already owns the shape of — the trigger, the concurrency, the secrets and the failure reporting:

- `.github/workflows/product.yml` — the `ship main` job (preflight → D1 migrations → deploy the Worker → build the site against the derived API origin → deploy the site → smoke). Its `checks` and `screen` jobs are the requirements suite on `pull_request`, which is a different question: decide deliberately whether those move too or stay as ordinary CI.
- `.github/workflows/provision.yml` — `workflow_dispatch`, creates whatever production is missing and commits the D1 id (#69).
- `.github/workflows/preflight.yml` — `workflow_dispatch`, reads production and reports.

Each is a `code_work` command with no cadence: the deploy fires on a merge to `main`, and provision and preflight are `frequency: 'manual'`, woken by whoever knows the event happened. The tools underneath (`npm run preflight`, `npm run provision`, `npm run deploy:api`, `npm run deploy:site`, `npm run smoke`) are already plain commands and shouldn't need to change — what moves is the wrapping.

The `writing-tasks` skill owns the contract each task is written to; read it before writing one.

Watch for two things the current workflows do that a task has to keep doing: the deploy threads a derived origin between steps through `GITHUB_ENV` (see `dev/tools/deploy.ts`), and `provision.yml` pushes the pinned D1 id to `main` with `contents: write` and no force. Whatever replaces them needs an equivalent for both, or a stated reason it doesn't.

**Done** = the deploy, provision and preflight paths run as Claudinite tasks, each watched to a terminal state in a forced run rather than left for its next natural trigger, and the workflow files they replace are deleted rather than left dormant beside them.

## 2. Record the rule

The owner wants a standing preference: **work that wants to run in CI becomes a Claudinite task, not a hand-authored GitHub Actions workflow.**

Before writing anything: the canon may already carry this. `claudinite-growth`'s RULES.md opens with *"Wanting a job to run in Actions — make it a task with a `code_work` command rather than authoring a workflow; the vendored workflows already own the trigger, the concurrency, the secrets and the failure reporting. Work with no cadence is a task too, on `frequency: 'manual'`, woken by whatever knows the event happened."* If that already says what the owner means, **write no new rule** — say so, and land only the residue that is genuinely this repo's (if any). Widening the canon entry belongs to the growth lifecycle, not to this run.

If a local rule is warranted, it goes in `.claudinite/local/packs/hitbut/RULES.md` and rides the mechanism promotion ladder — a check before prose, if one is expressible (e.g. a new file under `.github/workflows/` that is not one of the vendored Claudinite workflows). Author the assurance first and watch it fail.

Then it stops. Nothing checks that the thing it just shipped answers.

Two consequences:

**A deploy that passed CI can still be broken in production.** Everything the suite proves is proven against a local `workerd` with local D1, R2 and Queues (#28, item 1). A missing binding, an unapplied migration, a wrong `API_ORIGIN`, a Pages project pointing at the wrong output — every one of those is invisible to CI and fatal in production, and today the job goes green for all of them.

**There is no way back.** No step captures what was previously deployed, and nothing in the repo describes how to return to it. When the site is wrong at 2am the question "what do I do right now" has no answer written down.

## What to add

- **A smoke step, in the deploy job, after Pages** — fetch the deployed API and the deployed site and assert real content: `/api/v1/figures` returns 200 with an `items` array, `/api/v1/nope` returns the 404 envelope (proving it is our Worker and not a platform placeholder), and the site's root returns HTML containing the wordmark. Fail the job on any of them, so the run that shipped a broken deploy is red rather than green.
- **A rollback path, written down and exercised once.** Both Workers and Pages retain previous deployments; the exact mechanism needs checking against Cloudflare's docs (unreachable from the session that filed this) and then recording in the repo — with the version or deployment id of the previous good deploy logged by the job, so the answer at 2am is a command and not an investigation.

Note that a smoke test failing is *not* the same as a rollback happening. Order it deliberately: fail loudly first, automate the revert only once the failure signal is trusted.

The design doc carries the end state and the rationale; this issue carries only the phases and their exit conditions. Append-only once agreed.

**What changed and why.** v1 (#25) shipped a corpus of flat statements judged in pairs against a topic list read off the source. Three things break that at the scale now intended — decades of archives, many sources, a big roster: one speech carried by five outlets became five statements; pairwise judging is O(n²) and cannot see a trend at all; and a topic vocabulary decides in advance what the corpus may be about. The replacement is utterances with many attestations, subjects discovered by embedding, and a stance series per persona per subject.

**This is cheap now and expensive later.** The corpus is fixtures, so this is a rewrite of code and spec, not a migration of cited data. After the first real source it becomes the hard case the stable-id promise exists to prevent.

## Phases

**0. Provisioning (human-only, front-loaded)** — see the comment added to #27
- [ ] Vectorize index created and bound; Workflows enabled on the account.
- [ ] The embedding model and the stance model chosen, both reachable from the Worker.
- [ ] Exit: `wrangler deploy --dry-run` resolves the new bindings from the committed config.

**1. Verify the Workflow bet**
- [ ] Read Cloudflare's published step, duration and payload limits for Workflows and check a one-year archive slice against them. **They could not be read from the session that wrote the design** — the doc says so rather than asserting numbers.
- [ ] Exit: either a slice size that provably fits, or a recorded decision to slice smaller / move the stage.

**2. Spec first**
- [ ] Rewrite the affected leaves in `dev/requirements/requirements.md`: utterance vs attestation, date precision, roster resolution (#31), emergent clusters, stance, the two finding kinds. Watch the coverage gate go red before any case exists.
- [ ] Exit: the gate is red for exactly the new leaves, green once claimed.

**3. Data model**
- [ ] `utterances` + `attestations` replace `statements`; `said_at_precision`; `clusters`, `stances`, `findings`.
- [ ] Exit: logic cases prove one speech across three documents is one utterance and three attestations; that a month-precision date is neither a day nor unknown; that supersede-not-overwrite still holds for findings.

**4. Ingestion**
- [ ] The pipeline as one module — fetch, extract, resolve, merge, embed, assign, stance — every stage idempotent under retry.
- [ ] Exit: behavior cases prove a replayed payload writes nothing new, an unrostered speaker is retained unattributed, and the same quote at three lengths merges to one utterance.

**5. Embedding, clustering, stance**
- [ ] Vector store and stance model behind interfaces a case can script; online cluster assignment; stance stored with model and prompt version.
- [ ] Exit: cases over fixtures where the *source* topic strings deliberately disagree still cluster together (#33), and a scripted stance model produces a readable series.

**6. Detection**
- [ ] Anomaly (deviation from prevailing stance, carrying venue and audience) and trend change (change point, reported as an interval).
- [ ] Exit: cases over a synthetic series with a planted step change and a planted outlier find each, and find nothing in a flat series.

**7. Backfill Workflow**
- [ ] One run per archive slice, sharing the ingestion code, resumable per step.
- [ ] Exit: a slice runs end to end against fixtures; a deliberately failed step retries without re-fetching.

**8. API and site**
- [ ] `/api/v1` and the six pages carry utterances, attestations and findings. The inconsistency page keeps its shape: the two representative utterances either side of a change point.
- [ ] Exit: server and screen lanes green; goldens refreshed and reviewed.

Ordering: 0 and 1 front-loaded → 2 → 3 → 4 → {5, 6} → 7 → 8. Review lands as one stack, not a wait per phase.

## Out of scope

*Why* a trend changed — the design settles for when. Cross-persona comparison. Anything that would need a source we have not agreed to take.

What survives is stated here.*

A cluster is an emergent subject — the corpus discovers it, nobody chooses it in advance. `clusters.label` is `NULL` at creation and [`relabelCluster`](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/blob/main/src/backend/corpus/store.ts) is what sets it.

**Nothing calls `relabelCluster` outside the test tree.** Fixtures call it; one case calls it; no production path does. So on real data every cluster ships unnamed, `figureStats` returns subjects whose labels are all null, and the figure page renders no chips at all — its filter is `.filter(label => Boolean(label))`, which is the right behaviour (an unnamed subject shown as a placeholder would be worse) and currently filters out everything.

Nothing is broken. The product is simply missing a step, and the surface honestly shows nothing rather than pretending.

**What the step has to decide:**

- **What names a cluster.** The members are utterances that embed near each other; the name is a short human-readable phrase over them. That is a model call, so it is blocked on #27 along with the embedding and stance models. A non-model fallback — the most distinctive term shared across members — is cheap and would be wrong often enough to be worth deciding deliberately rather than defaulting into.
- **When it runs.** A label over three members is a worse name than one over thirty, and members keep arriving. `relabelCluster` exists precisely so a name can be replaced; the schema comment already says nothing keys on the label, so relabelling moves nothing. What is undecided is the trigger — a threshold, a cadence, or a pass over clusters whose membership changed.
- **Whether an unnamed cluster should be visible at all.** Findings reference clusters by id and read fine unnamed. The figure page's chips do not. Those may want different answers.
- **What a leaf would assert.** Probably: a cluster with enough members carries a label, and the figure page shows it as a chip — which is a screen-kind leaf over a seeded corpus, not a logic one, because the claim is about what the reader sees.

Not urgent while the corpus is fixtures, which name their clusters by hand. It becomes visible the moment real data lands, because that is when the first cluster nobody named reaches the page.

This is that work. The roster it feeds is #31; the two must land together, because the first crawl is when an unrostered speaker first appears.

## The pair to start with, and why it is a pair

An inconsistency needs two moments about one topic, so two archives of the same era buy nothing. The minimum useful combination is one deep historical source and one current one, covering the same people:

1. **Knesset plenum and committee protocols — the "then".** Verbatim, attributed, dated, officially published, decades deep, and no contract to breach. Nothing else in Israeli public life gives all four for free.
2. **One current official feed — the "now".** gov.il and ministry announcements, or party press feeds. Announcement prose needs care on attribution: "the ministry said" is not "the minister said", and only the latter is a statement by a figure.

Deliberately **not** in the first pass: press interviews and op-eds (highest value for a stated position shift, worst on ToS and bot walls — they follow the legal review), broadcast (needs ASR), and social platforms. The last is not a scheduling call: the competitor-landscape wiki's clearest finding is that platform-API dependence is the top cause of death in this space — it killed both politician-tweet archives.

## Backfill window

**The current Knesset plus the previous one** — roughly four to six years. Far enough back that positions have genuinely moved, and a bounded job with an end, rather than an open-ended crawl. Ongoing coverage then runs on the cron, and the per-source `refreshMinutes` already in the registry carries the asymmetry: a protocol archive and a press feed do not move at the same speed.

## Reconnaissance needs a sanctioned home

**It cannot be done from an agent session.** The sandbox's egress policy denies `knesset.gov.il`, `www.gov.il` and `oknesset.org` outright — `403` to CONNECT at the proxy, a policy denial rather than a bot wall — and routing around a policy boundary is not on the table.

So the recon gets one home, which is also the shape the web-scraping rules ask for:

- [ ] A `workflow_dispatch` job on a GitHub runner that fetches a named list of candidate URLs and **commits the raw payloads** as sample fixtures.
- [ ] The `map-a-data-source` recon then runs **offline against those committed bytes**: locate the real data surface in the preferred order — a hydration blob, then a client API, then the markup — and write the findings into a reference doc beside the source module, complete enough that no question about the service needs a second probe.
- [ ] The parser and its per-source case are written against the same committed sample, so the extractor tests need no network and a parser fix costs no requests.
- [ ] Each source module declares its data surface and its refresh clock at registration, which the registry already enforces (`3.7`).

A datacenter IP being blocked is the expected failure here, not a surprise. If a source stays blocked from a runner, the answer is a commercial rendering proxy with the credential in repository secrets — one config-level decision in the fetch module, never a per-scraper workaround.

## Exit

The first two sources each have: a committed real sample, a reference doc, a registered module, and a passing case reading owner-reviewed expected values off the committed bytes. At that point the supported-source matrix becomes spec — each supported source its own leaf — and dropping one becomes a visible change rather than a silent regression.

Blocked on nothing. Needs #31's roster to land alongside it.

Green means every leaf is *claimed by a passing case of the right kind* — these are the places where that is honestly less than "verified in the world". Each is a burn-down item, not a caveat to live with.

**Four gaps are open.**

**1. The platform is a local one.** Server- and screen-kind cases run the shipped Worker on the real `workerd` runtime under Miniflare, against local D1 and R2. They confirm our code *asks* Cloudflare for the right thing — they do not confirm Cloudflare *performs* it: no real D1 (only the same SQLite engine), no real R2 durability, no edge cache, and no Workflow (the backfill's runner is a harness). Closes with #27 plus the post-deploy smoke #36 tracks.

**2. Requirement `7.1` is provisional.** "A merge to `main` reaches the deployed site with no human build step" cannot be asserted from a test at all; it is listed in `dev/requirements/provisional.json` so the coverage gate lets it stand unclaimed, and it is the one entry there. It burns down when provisioning lands and a merge is observed end to end.

**3. No embedding or stance model has been chosen, let alone evaluated for Hebrew.** This is what the old "the judge model is unevaluated for Hebrew" gap *became* — see the comment below. The pipeline runs against scripted fakes, which prove merge/embed/assign/place and the stored trail, and say nothing about judgment quality. A stance model placing Hebrew political speech on an axis is at least as sensitive to the language as a pairwise judge was. Blocked on #27; the model is a config value behind one interface, so a swap is not a rewrite.

**4. There is no supported-source matrix yet.** Acquisition and backfill are proven against a fixture source, which proves the machinery (raw-before-parse, retry policy, bot-wall detection, batch isolation, slice independence) and nothing about any real site. Real sources need a `map-a-data-source` recon and the owner's pick (#32); inventing a sample would prove support for a target the world does not serve, so none was invented.

**Two gaps have left this list.**

- **Israeli defamation law was unreviewed.** It has been reviewed. #54 landed what it requires: one written inclusion rule in `data/roster.json` that every entry must state how it meets, every quote naming the publication that carried it, and the detection caveat on the finding page itself. Until real people are in the roster, every figure in it is invented.
- **The pairwise judge is moot rather than closed.** #53 removed it; the concern moved into gap 3 above.

## 1. Convert the deploy workflows to Claudinite tasks

The repo hand-authors three workflows that Claudinite's vendored plumbing already owns the shape of — the trigger, the concurrency, the secrets and the failure reporting:

- `.github/workflows/product.yml` — the `ship main` job (preflight → D1 migrations → deploy the Worker → build the site against the derived API origin → deploy the site → smoke). Its `checks` and `screen` jobs are the requirements suite on `pull_request`, which is a different question: decide deliberately whether those move too or stay as ordinary CI.
- `.github/workflows/provision.yml` — `workflow_dispatch`, creates whatever production is missing and commits the D1 id (#69).
- `.github/workflows/preflight.yml` — `workflow_dispatch`, reads production and reports.

Each is a `code_work` command with no cadence: the deploy fires on a merge to `main`, and provision and preflight are `frequency: 'manual'`, woken by whoever knows the event happened. The tools underneath (`npm run preflight`, `npm run provision`, `npm run deploy:api`, `npm run deploy:site`, `npm run smoke`) are already plain commands and shouldn't need to change — what moves is the wrapping.

The `writing-tasks` skill owns the contract each task is written to; read it before writing one.

Watch for two things the current workflows do that a task has to keep doing: the deploy threads a derived origin between steps through `GITHUB_ENV` (see `dev/tools/deploy.ts`), and `provision.yml` pushes the pinned D1 id to `main` with `contents: write` and no force. Whatever replaces them needs an equivalent for both, or a stated reason it doesn't.

**Done** = the deploy, provision and preflight paths run as Claudinite tasks, each watched to a terminal state in a forced run rather than left for its next natural trigger, and the workflow files they replace are deleted rather than left dormant beside them.

## 2. Record the rule

The owner wants a standing preference: **work that wants to run in CI becomes a Claudinite task, not a hand-authored GitHub Actions workflow.**

Before writing anything: the canon may already carry this. `claudinite-growth`'s RULES.md opens with *"Wanting a job to run in Actions — make it a task with a `code_work` command rather than authoring a workflow; the vendored workflows already own the trigger, the concurrency, the secrets and the failure reporting. Work with no cadence is a task too, on `frequency: 'manual'`, woken by whatever knows the event happened."* If that already says what the owner means, **write no new rule** — say so, and land only the residue that is genuinely this repo's (if any). Widening the canon entry belongs to the growth lifecycle, not to this run.

If a local rule is warranted, it goes in `.claudinite/local/packs/hitbut/RULES.md` and rides the mechanism promotion ladder — a check before prose, if one is expressible (e.g. a new file under `.github/workflows/` that is not one of the vendored Claudinite workflows). Author the assurance first and watch it fail.

This repo evidenced a new Claudinite canon pack in this week's fleet sweep — it is the first

- `src/backend/README.md` — `env.ts` hand-declares the platform methods this Worker uses instead

- `docs/architecture/DESIGN.md` — the deploy applies D1 migrations before it replaces the Worker

- `dev/requirements/server/run.test.ts` + `dev/requirements/shared/worker-config.ts` — the
  `wrangler` package's `createTestHarness` driving the real committed `wrangler.toml` against real
  `workerd`, and why the `[ai]` binding used to force an authenticated proxy under test.
- `dev/requirements/shared/migrations.ts` — seeding a test's D1 from the shipped `.sql` migration
  files rather than a hand-written test schema.
- `dev/tools/smoke.ts` / `dev/tools/preflight.ts` — local Wrangler emulation not proving
  Cloudflare's own D1/R2/Queues (issue #28), and telling a Wrangler preflight's *missing* apart
  from *unknown* by parsing its own `✘`/`▲` error markers.

**Canon PR:** missingbulb/Claudinite#1284

**Blocker:** nothing to do yet. Declaring `cloudflare-workers` now would be a blocking `config`
error — the pack's code isn't on disk here until that PR merges *and* this repo's next Claudinite
converge picks it up.

**Once both hold:** run the `adopt-pack` skill (declares it, asks its adoption questions,
re-vendors).

Then it stops. Nothing checks that the thing it just shipped answers.

Two consequences:

**A deploy that passed CI can still be broken in production.** Everything the suite proves is proven against a local `workerd` with local D1, R2 and Queues (#28, item 1). A missing binding, an unapplied migration, a wrong `API_ORIGIN`, a Pages project pointing at the wrong output — every one of those is invisible to CI and fatal in production, and today the job goes green for all of them.

**There is no way back.** No step captures what was previously deployed, and nothing in the repo describes how to return to it. When the site is wrong at 2am the question "what do I do right now" has no answer written down.

## What to add

- **A smoke step, in the deploy job, after Pages** — fetch the deployed API and the deployed site and assert real content: `/api/v1/figures` returns 200 with an `items` array, `/api/v1/nope` returns the 404 envelope (proving it is our Worker and not a platform placeholder), and the site's root returns HTML containing the wordmark. Fail the job on any of them, so the run that shipped a broken deploy is red rather than green.
- **A rollback path, written down and exercised once.** Both Workers and Pages retain previous deployments; the exact mechanism needs checking against Cloudflare's docs (unreachable from the session that filed this) and then recording in the repo — with the version or deployment id of the previous good deploy logged by the job, so the answer at 2am is a command and not an investigation.

Note that a smoke test failing is *not* the same as a rollback happening. Order it deliberately: fail loudly first, automate the revert only once the failure signal is trusted.

The design doc carries the end state and the rationale; this issue carries only the phases and their exit conditions. Append-only once agreed.

**What changed and why.** v1 (#25) shipped a corpus of flat statements judged in pairs against a topic list read off the source. Three things break that at the scale now intended — decades of archives, many sources, a big roster: one speech carried by five outlets became five statements; pairwise judging is O(n²) and cannot see a trend at all; and a topic vocabulary decides in advance what the corpus may be about. The replacement is utterances with many attestations, subjects discovered by embedding, and a stance series per persona per subject.

**This is cheap now and expensive later.** The corpus is fixtures, so this is a rewrite of code and spec, not a migration of cited data. After the first real source it becomes the hard case the stable-id promise exists to prevent.

## Phases

**0. Provisioning (human-only, front-loaded)** — see the comment added to #27
- [ ] Vectorize index created and bound; Workflows enabled on the account.
- [ ] The embedding model and the stance model chosen, both reachable from the Worker.
- [ ] Exit: `wrangler deploy --dry-run` resolves the new bindings from the committed config.

**1. Verify the Workflow bet**
- [ ] Read Cloudflare's published step, duration and payload limits for Workflows and check a one-year archive slice against them. **They could not be read from the session that wrote the design** — the doc says so rather than asserting numbers.
- [ ] Exit: either a slice size that provably fits, or a recorded decision to slice smaller / move the stage.

**2. Spec first**
- [ ] Rewrite the affected leaves in `dev/requirements/requirements.md`: utterance vs attestation, date precision, roster resolution (#31), emergent clusters, stance, the two finding kinds. Watch the coverage gate go red before any case exists.
- [ ] Exit: the gate is red for exactly the new leaves, green once claimed.

**3. Data model**
- [ ] `utterances` + `attestations` replace `statements`; `said_at_precision`; `clusters`, `stances`, `findings`.
- [ ] Exit: logic cases prove one speech across three documents is one utterance and three attestations; that a month-precision date is neither a day nor unknown; that supersede-not-overwrite still holds for findings.

**4. Ingestion**
- [ ] The pipeline as one module — fetch, extract, resolve, merge, embed, assign, stance — every stage idempotent under retry.
- [ ] Exit: behavior cases prove a replayed payload writes nothing new, an unrostered speaker is retained unattributed, and the same quote at three lengths merges to one utterance.

**5. Embedding, clustering, stance**
- [ ] Vector store and stance model behind interfaces a case can script; online cluster assignment; stance stored with model and prompt version.
- [ ] Exit: cases over fixtures where the *source* topic strings deliberately disagree still cluster together (#33), and a scripted stance model produces a readable series.

**6. Detection**
- [ ] Anomaly (deviation from prevailing stance, carrying venue and audience) and trend change (change point, reported as an interval).
- [ ] Exit: cases over a synthetic series with a planted step change and a planted outlier find each, and find nothing in a flat series.

**7. Backfill Workflow**
- [ ] One run per archive slice, sharing the ingestion code, resumable per step.
- [ ] Exit: a slice runs end to end against fixtures; a deliberately failed step retries without re-fetching.

**8. API and site**
- [ ] `/api/v1` and the six pages carry utterances, attestations and findings. The inconsistency page keeps its shape: the two representative utterances either side of a change point.
- [ ] Exit: server and screen lanes green; goldens refreshed and reviewed.

Ordering: 0 and 1 front-loaded → 2 → 3 → 4 → {5, 6} → 7 → 8. Review lands as one stack, not a wait per phase.

## Out of scope

*Why* a trend changed — the design settles for when. Cross-persona comparison. Anything that would need a source we have not agreed to take.

What survives is stated here.*

A cluster is an emergent subject — the corpus discovers it, nobody chooses it in advance. `clusters.label` is `NULL` at creation and [`relabelCluster`](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/blob/main/src/backend/corpus/store.ts) is what sets it.

**Nothing calls `relabelCluster` outside the test tree.** Fixtures call it; one case calls it; no production path does. So on real data every cluster ships unnamed, `figureStats` returns subjects whose labels are all null, and the figure page renders no chips at all — its filter is `.filter(label => Boolean(label))`, which is the right behaviour (an unnamed subject shown as a placeholder would be worse) and currently filters out everything.

Nothing is broken. The product is simply missing a step, and the surface honestly shows nothing rather than pretending.

**What the step has to decide:**

- **What names a cluster.** The members are utterances that embed near each other; the name is a short human-readable phrase over them. That is a model call, so it is blocked on #27 along with the embedding and stance models. A non-model fallback — the most distinctive term shared across members — is cheap and would be wrong often enough to be worth deciding deliberately rather than defaulting into.
- **When it runs.** A label over three members is a worse name than one over thirty, and members keep arriving. `relabelCluster` exists precisely so a name can be replaced; the schema comment already says nothing keys on the label, so relabelling moves nothing. What is undecided is the trigger — a threshold, a cadence, or a pass over clusters whose membership changed.
- **Whether an unnamed cluster should be visible at all.** Findings reference clusters by id and read fine unnamed. The figure page's chips do not. Those may want different answers.
- **What a leaf would assert.** Probably: a cluster with enough members carries a label, and the figure page shows it as a chip — which is a screen-kind leaf over a seeded corpus, not a logic one, because the claim is about what the reader sees.

Not urgent while the corpus is fixtures, which name their clusters by hand. It becomes visible the moment real data lands, because that is when the first cluster nobody named reaches the page.

This is that work. The roster it feeds is #31; the two must land together, because the first crawl is when an unrostered speaker first appears.

## The pair to start with, and why it is a pair

An inconsistency needs two moments about one topic, so two archives of the same era buy nothing. The minimum useful combination is one deep historical source and one current one, covering the same people:

1. **Knesset plenum and committee protocols — the "then".** Verbatim, attributed, dated, officially published, decades deep, and no contract to breach. Nothing else in Israeli public life gives all four for free.
2. **One current official feed — the "now".** gov.il and ministry announcements, or party press feeds. Announcement prose needs care on attribution: "the ministry said" is not "the minister said", and only the latter is a statement by a figure.

Deliberately **not** in the first pass: press interviews and op-eds (highest value for a stated position shift, worst on ToS and bot walls — they follow the legal review), broadcast (needs ASR), and social platforms. The last is not a scheduling call: the competitor-landscape wiki's clearest finding is that platform-API dependence is the top cause of death in this space — it killed both politician-tweet archives.

## Backfill window

**The current Knesset plus the previous one** — roughly four to six years. Far enough back that positions have genuinely moved, and a bounded job with an end, rather than an open-ended crawl. Ongoing coverage then runs on the cron, and the per-source `refreshMinutes` already in the registry carries the asymmetry: a protocol archive and a press feed do not move at the same speed.

## Reconnaissance needs a sanctioned home

**It cannot be done from an agent session.** The sandbox's egress policy denies `knesset.gov.il`, `www.gov.il` and `oknesset.org` outright — `403` to CONNECT at the proxy, a policy denial rather than a bot wall — and routing around a policy boundary is not on the table.

So the recon gets one home, which is also the shape the web-scraping rules ask for:

- [ ] A `workflow_dispatch` job on a GitHub runner that fetches a named list of candidate URLs and **commits the raw payloads** as sample fixtures.
- [ ] The `map-a-data-source` recon then runs **offline against those committed bytes**: locate the real data surface in the preferred order — a hydration blob, then a client API, then the markup — and write the findings into a reference doc beside the source module, complete enough that no question about the service needs a second probe.
- [ ] The parser and its per-source case are written against the same committed sample, so the extractor tests need no network and a parser fix costs no requests.
- [ ] Each source module declares its data surface and its refresh clock at registration, which the registry already enforces (`3.7`).

A datacenter IP being blocked is the expected failure here, not a surprise. If a source stays blocked from a runner, the answer is a commercial rendering proxy with the credential in repository secrets — one config-level decision in the fetch module, never a per-scraper workaround.

## Exit

The first two sources each have: a committed real sample, a reference doc, a registered module, and a passing case reading owner-reviewed expected values off the committed bytes. At that point the supported-source matrix becomes spec — each supported source its own leaf — and dropping one becomes a visible change rather than a silent regression.

Blocked on nothing. Needs #31's roster to land alongside it.

Now researched against Israeli sources first-hand, and the findings are load-bearing for [#32](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/32): Copyright Act 5768-2007 §6 puts Knesset proceedings **outside copyright entirely**; the Knesset OData service is **open and keyless**, 38 collections; and each sitting is published **twice** — the edited record and the stenogram — and *the two texts differ*. That last one is the same trap the C-SPAN pass found in the Congressional Record, now confirmed for the source you'd actually build on. Also found `knesset-ai.com`, the closest live competitor in any market.

**[#97](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/pull/97) — "Refuse to guess where the API is."** The operator console reported "404 from /status" because an unset origin fell back to a relative URL that resolved against its own host — a setting nobody had filled in, arriving disguised as the API refusing. **[#99](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/pull/99) — the wordmark.** התבט carved worn, אויות lacquered; every screen golden re-rendered. The screen lane also gained the ability to capture one element's box, so a leaf about the masthead is proven by a picture of the masthead.

The executor workflow's `# claudinite:secrets` marker had nothing stamped under it, so `CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN` never reached the job. The corrected workflow already existed, staged at `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` — but a converge can't write `.github/workflows/`, so it withholds the file, and **the only thing that delivers a staged workflow is the agent stage that couldn't start without the token the staged file carried.** The repo could not escape on its own. # Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it again.
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.

{"id":32713583992,"name":"product","display_title":"Ask the account where a Worker would even be published","workflow_id":339572729,"run_number":76,"run_attempt":1,"event":"pull_request","status":"in_progress","head_branch":"claude/issue-27-resource-creation-qxprdo","head_sha":"8c6426041e34c7d6e9e13c52f2b8c4bb10f513bf","head_commit":{"message":"Ask the account where a Worker would even be published

The deploy reached production, applied the migrations, and then failed: the
account has never registered a workers.dev subdomain, so `wrangler deploy` had
nowhere to publish to. It asks for one interactively, and on a runner that is a
failed deploy — after the schema has already moved.

The preflight said production was ready, because it only ever asked wrangler,
and wrangler has no command for this. It now reads the account directly for the
subdomain — a GET, the only one here, and the whole reason the wrangler runner
stays closed to everything else.

The failure that led here also arrived with its actionable half missing: the
URL wrangler sends you to sits after a blank line, and the reason stopped at the
first one. It now crosses a single blank and stops at two.

input.commit_title: Ask the account where a Worker would even be published (#89)
input.commit_message:
The deploy reached production, applied the migrations, and then failed: the
account had never registered a workers.dev subdomain, so `wrangler deploy` had
nowhere to publish to. It asks for one interactively, and on a runner that is a
failed deploy — after the schema has already moved.

The preflight said production was ready, because it only ever asked wrangler,
and wrangler has no command for this. It now reads the account directly for the
subdomain — a GET, the only one here, and the whole reason the wrangler runner
stays closed to everything else.

The failure that led here also arrived with its actionable half missing: the
URL wrangler sends you to sits after a blank line, and the reason stopped at the
first one. It now crosses a single blank and stops at two.

Refs #27
